react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway analysis of eight structurally non-redundant metabolites reveals two robust, cross-validated biological signals. First, Selenium (KEGG:C01529, elemental selenium atom, ChEBI:27568) is the sole driver of three significantly enriched WikiPathways: Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=1.1×10⁻³), the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=2.1×10⁻³), and Pluripotent stem cell differentiation (WP:WP2848, FDR=7.2×10⁻⁴). Selenium is a cofactor for glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), the enzyme that prevents lipid peroxidation and is the central mechanistic node of ferroptosis — a iron-dependent, non-apoptotic cell death pathway. Disruption of selenium bioavailability directly impairs GPX4 function, predisposing cells to ferroptotic death. Second, Thromboxane A₂ (KEGG:C02198, ChEBI:15627) is the ranked-1 hit in MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (mummichog p=0.00235) and appears as a member in HUMAN1:eicosanoid_metabolism alongside the broader prostaglandin/leukotriene family (PGD₂, PGE₂, PGI₂, TXB₂, LXA₄, LXB₄). The co-enrichment of thromboxane with multiple downstream prostaglandins under a single significant pathway node reflects activation of the COX-mediated arachidonate cascade. Cross-paradigm convergence is strong: mummichog additionally recovers arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p=0.0136) in its top-10, confirming the same lipid mediator axis. The D-Glucose signal (KEGG:C00221) drives four glucose-centric mummichog hits (glycolysis, N-glycan biosynthesis, hexose phosphorylation, sialic acid metabolism) at identical p=0.0136, consistent with metabolic reprogramming secondary to oxidative stress. Methimazole (ChEBI:50673), a thionamide used to treat hyperthyroidism, is consistent with perturbation of the selenium-iodide axis in thyroid hormone synthesis. The absence of ID conflicts (0 structural disagreements across 8 InChIKeys) confirms that all eight inputs are genuine, distinct metabolites.

This mummichog result reflects mass-based matching and captures lipid mediators even when standard ID resolution is incomplete. The same mummichog analysis also identified multiple glucose-centric pathways (N-glycan biosynthesis, glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, sialic acid metabolism, hexose phosphorylation, and fructose and mannose metabolism) all sharing identical p=0.0165; the co-incident p-values reflect shared network topology around D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) rather than independent biological signals. In contrast, the RaMP ORA analysis resolved only the selenium input (KEGG:C01529), which drove enrichment of three WikiPathways: pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (FDR=7.2×10⁻⁴), ferroptosis (FDR=1.1×10⁻³), and selenium micronutrient network (FDR=2.1×10⁻³). The divergence between the mummichog and RaMP results reflects the differential ability of mass-based versus ID-based matching to resolve the eight input metabolites. No structural InChIKey conflicts were detected across the eight inputs.

First, Selenium (KEGG:C01529, elemental selenium atom, ChEBI:27568) is the sole driver of three significantly enriched WikiPathways: Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=1.1×10⁻³), the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=2.1×10⁻³), and Pluripotent stem cell differentiation (WP:WP2848, FDR=7.2×10⁻⁴). Selenium is a cofactor for glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), the enzyme that prevents lipid peroxidation and is the central mechanistic node of ferroptosis — a iron-dependent, non-apoptotic cell death pathway. Disruption of selenium bioavailability directly impairs GPX4 function, predisposing cells to ferroptotic death. Second, Thromboxane A₂ (KEGG:C02198, ChEBI:15627) is the ranked-1 hit in MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (mummichog p=0.00235) and appears as a member in HUMAN1:eicosanoid_metabolism alongside the broader prostaglandin/leukotriene family (PGD₂, PGE₂, PGI₂, TXB₂, LXA₄, LXB₄). The co-enrichment of thromboxane with multiple downstream prostaglandins under a single significant pathway node reflects activation of the COX-mediated arachidonate cascade. Methimazole (ChEBI:50673), a thionamide used to treat hyperthyroidism, is consistent with perturbation of the selenium-iodide axis in thyroid hormone synthesis. The absence of ID conflicts (0 structural disagreements across 8 InChIKeys) confirms that all eight inputs are genuine, distinct metabolites.
